data.name: Qutub
data.gender_notes: Qutub is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A qutub is a pillar or axis that provides support and stability. In Islamic tradition, it refers to the axis of the universe, around which the heavens and earth rotate. The name Qutub carries the meaning “Axis, pillar” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Qutub usually hope their child will grow to embody axis, pillar and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic mysticism, the Qutub is considered to be the axis of divine love and the source of spiritual guidance.
data.etymology: Qutub belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Axis, pillar.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Qutub total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: قُطب
in_arabic.long_meaning: قُطب هو مصطلح عربي يعني الزعيم أو القائد، ويُستخدم في الإسلام لوصف شخص يمتلك صفات قيادية وروحية عالية، وقد استخدم هذا المصطلح في التاريخ الإسلامي لوصف أعلام الدين والقادة الروحيين، وله أهمية كبيرة في الثقافة الإسلامية

in_urdu.name: قطب

in_english.name: Qutub
in_english.long_meaning: Qutub is an Arabic term meaning leader or spiritual guide, used in Islam to describe a person with high leadership and spiritual qualities, it has significant importance in Islamic culture and history, and is used to describe prominent religious figures and spiritual leaders

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic architecture, the word qutub is used to describe a monumental pillar that often forms the central point, both structurally and symbolically, around which a mosque or mausoleum is built. These pillars have been instrumental in defining the aesthetic and architectural style of Islamic structures, and many famous mosques, such as the Qutub Minar in India, bear the name as a mark of their historical and cultural significance.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the term qutub holds deep significance as a symbol of stability, strength, and guidance. It is believed that God has appointed certain individuals as qutubs or spiritual leaders to guide humans on the path to spiritual growth and enlightenment. These individuals are considered to be the 'axes' around which their communities revolve, and their teachings and wisdom serve as a source of inspiration and support. Thus, the name 'Qutub' serves as a reminder of the essential role that spiritual leaders and pillars of faith play in our lives.
